title: FRAMEWORK ACT ON PROMOTION OF DATA INDUSTRY AND DATA UTILIZATION
title_original: 데이터 산업진흥 및 이용촉진에 관한 기본법
full_text:
CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of this Act is to prescribe matters necessary for promoting the production, transaction, and utilization of data, thereby creating economic value from data and establishing a foundation for the development of the data industry, so as to contribute to the improvement of the lives of the people and the development of the national economy.

Article 2 (Definitions) The terms used in this Act are defined as follows:
  1. "Data" means materials or information that can be processed by optical or electronic means and that is obtained through observation, experimentation, investigation, collection, etc., or generated through information systems and software as defined in subparagraph 1 of Article 2 of the Software Promotion Act, for the purpose of creating diverse added value;
  2. "Public data" means public data as defined in subparagraph 2 of Article 2 of the Act on Promotion of the Provision and Use of Public Data;
  3. "Private data" means data generated or acquired and managed by a person other than a State agency, a local government, or a public institution (referring to a public institution defined in subparagraph 16 of Article 2 of the Framework Act on Intelligent Informatization; hereinafter the same shall apply);
  4. "Data producer" means a person engaged in economic activities related to the generation, processing, creation, etc. of data;
  5. "Data industry" means an industry that provides services and performs activities related to a series of processes, including the production, distribution, transaction, and utilization of data, for the purpose of creating economic added value;
  6. "Data service provider" means a person engaged in the data industry;
  7. "Data transaction service provider" means a data service provider whose business consists of directly selling data or intermediating data transactions between parties seeking to sell data and parties seeking to purchase data;
  8. "Data analytics service provider" means a data service provider that engages in the business of providing information generated through the collection, combination, processing, integration, and analysis of data.

Article 3 (Responsibilities of the State) (1) The State and local governments shall endeavor to establish a foundation for facilitating the data production, transaction, and utilization.
  (2) The State and local governments may promote the domestic and cross-border transfer of data to the extent necessary for facilitating data production, transaction, and utilization.
  (3) The State and local governments shall respect the creativity of the private sector and endeavor to enable market-driven decision-making.
  (4) The State and local governments shall endeavor to promote the utilization and protection of intellectual property rights defined in subparagraph 3 of Article 3 of the Framework Act on Intellectual Property, and personal information defined in subparagraph 1 of Article 2 of the Personal Information Protection Act.
  (5) The State and local governments shall endeavor to promote mutually beneficial cooperation and harmonious development among large enterprises, small and medium enterprises, and venture businesses in the data industry.
  (6) The State and local governments shall endeavor to minimize any regulation that impedes the facilitation of data production, transaction, and utilization.

Article 4 (Master plans) (1) The Government shall formulate a master plan for the promotion of the data industry (hereinafter referred to as "master plan") every 3 years after consultation with the heads of relevant central administrative agencies in order to facilitate data production, transaction, and utilization and establish a foundation for the data industry.
  (2) The master plan shall be finalized after deliberation by the National Data Policy Committee under Article 6.
  (3) The master plan shall include the following; in such cases, matters regarding the facilitation of the generation, collection, management, and utilization of public data shall reflect the master plans formulated in accordance with the Act on Promotion of the Provision and Use of Public Data and the Act on the Promotion of Data-Based Administration:
  1. The basic direction for policy measures to promote the production, transaction, and utilization of data;
  2. Matters regarding the production and protection of data;
  3. Matters regarding the facilitation of data transactions;
  4. Matters regarding the promotion of data utilization;
  5. Matters regarding the training of data professionals;
  6. Matters regarding the establishment of a foundation for the data industry;
  7. Matters regarding the fostering of data service providers and data-specialized enterprises, such as support for startup and growth in the data industry, and special support for small and medium enterprises under Article 31;
  8. Matters regarding support for international cooperation related to the data industry;
  9. Matters regarding data-related plans formulated and operated under other statutes;
  10. Other matters prescribed by Presidential Decree for the promotion of the data industry.
  (4) Except as provided in paragraphs (1) through (3), matters necessary for the formulation and implementation of master plans shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 5 (Implementation plans) (1) The Minister of Science and ICT shall formulate an annual implementation plan for the promotion of the data industry (hereinafter referred to as "implementation plan") based on the master plan. In such cases, the Minister shall consult with the Minister of the Interior and Safety on matters regarding public data.
  (2) The implementation plan shall be finalized after deliberation by the National Data Policy Committee under Article 6.
  (3) The Minister of Science and ICT may request the heads of relevant central administrative agencies or the heads of local governments to provide materials necessary for formulating the implementation plan under paragraph (1).
  (4) Except as provided in paragraphs (1) through (3), matters necessary for the formulation, implementation, and other execution of the implementation plan shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 6 (National Data Policy Committee) (1) A National Data Policy Committee shall be established under the Prime Minister to deliberate on the following matters related to the promotion of data production, transaction, and utilization (hereafter in this Chapter referred to as the "Committee"):
  1. Matters regarding the formulation and implementation of master plans and implementation plans;
  2. Matters regarding the improvement of policies and systems related to data production, transaction, and utilization;
  3. Matters regarding the general supervision and coordination of policies for the promotion the data industry and of plans for the promotion of the data industry formulated and implemented under other statutes;
  4. Matters regarding the evaluation and review of the implementation results of the major policy measures in the master plan and implementation plan;
  5. Other matters deemed necessary by the chairperson.
  (2) The Committee shall consist of up to 30 members, including 1 Chairperson.
  (3) The Prime Minister shall serve as the Chairperson, and the members shall be the persons specified in the following subparagraphs: <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
  1. The Minister of Finance and Economy, the Minister of Science and ICT, the Minister of Education, the Minister of Interior and Safety, the Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism, the Minister of Trade, Industry and Resources, the Minister of Health and Welfare, the Minister of Employment and Labor, the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, the Minister of SMEs and Startups, the chairperson of the Korea Media and Communications Commission, the Chairperson of Fair Trade Commission, the Chairperson of Financial Services Commission, and the Chairperson of Personal Information Protection Commission;
  2. Persons commissioned by the Chairperson from among those who have extensive expertise and experience in the data industry.
  (4) The term of office of each member under paragraph (3)2 shall be 2 years and may be renewed only once.
  (5) The Committee shall have 2 executive secretary members, to be the Minister of Science and ICT and the Minister of the Interior and Safety.
  (6) A secretariat may be established within the Ministry of Science and ICT to support the activities of the Committee and handle its administrative affairs.
  (7) Except as provided in paragraphs (1) through (6), matters necessary for the composition and operation of the Committee and the secretariat shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  [Enforcement date: Jan. 2, 2026]

Article 7 (Relationship to other statutes) (1) Except as otherwise provided in other statutes, matters relating to the facilitation of data production, transaction, and utilization of data shall be governed by this Act.
  (2) Matters relating to personal information, copyrights, and public data shall be governed by the respective provisions of other statutes, including the Personal Information Protection Act, the Copyright Act, and the Act on Promotion of Provision and Use of Public Data.

Article 8 (Securing financial resources) The Government shall endeavor to secure financial resources necessary for facilitating data production, transaction, and utilization and for promoting the data industry.

CHAPTER II DATA PRODUCTION, UTILIZATION, AND PROTECTION

Article 9 (Promotion of data production) (1) The Government shall create an environment in which data and data products of various sectors and types can be producted, and shall establish policy measures to enhance the expertise of data producers and strengthen their competitiveness.
  (2) The Government may provide financial and technical support to data producers necessary for data production.
  (3) The Government shall endeavor to establish an institutional foundation to promote the development and research of data or data products through the shared utilization of personnel, facilities, materials, funds, and information.
  (4) The head of each relevant central administrative agency shall incorporate the sector- and type-specific data production promotion policy measures established under paragraph (1) into the implementation plan, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 10 (Facilitation of data combination) (1) The Minister of Science and ICT and the Minister of the Interior and Safety shall prepare and promote necessary policy measures such as exchanges between industries and the establishment of a convergence foundation with other fields to promote the production of new data through the combination of data.
  (2) The Minister of Science and ICT and the Minister of the Interior and Safety shall prepare exchange and cooperation plans to promote the combination of public and private data.
  (3) The Minister of Science and ICT may provide the following support to facilitate the combination of data under paragraphs (1) and (2):
  1. Development and implementation of cooperative education programs between domestic and foreign research institutes, universities, and companies;
  2. Promotion of the exchange of data professionals across industries;
  3. Projects for the transaction and utilization of combined data;
  4. Funds for those who conduct the relevant project;
  5. Other matters necessary for the combination of data and the vitalization of convergence thereof.
  (4) Matters necessary for the details of the formulation and promotion of policy measures under paragraph (1), a plan for exchange and cooperation under paragraph (2), and support, etc. under paragraph (3) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 11 (Designation of data safe zones) (1) The Minister of Science and ICT and the head of a relevant central administrative agency may designate and operate an area in which anyone can safely analyze and utilize data (hereinafter referred to as "data safe zone").
  (2) The Minister of Science and ICT and the head of a central administrative agency may provide support, including undisclosed data, and analytical systems and tools, in order to support the use of data safe zones.
  (3) The Minister of Science and ICT and the head of a relevant central administrative agency may request the Government, local governments, public institutions, private corporations, etc. to provide data if necessary for supporting the provision of undisclosed data under paragraph (2).
  (4) The Minister of Science and ICT and the head of a central administrative agency may provide technical and financial support necessary for providing data under paragraph (3).
  (5) The Minister of Science and ICT and the heads of relevant central administrative agencies shall establish and implement technical, physical, and administrative security measures, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, against any unlawful access, alteration, damage, leakage, or destruction by a third party of data within a data safe zone, or any other risks to the data safe zone.
  (6) Except as provided in paragraphs (1) through (5), matters necessary for the designation procedures, operation, etc. of data safe zones shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 12 (Protection of data assets) (1) Data that have economic value generated through substantial human or material investment and effort by a data producer (hereinafter referred to as "data assets") shall be protected.
  (2) No person shall infringe upon the economic interests of a data producer by misappropriating the data assets under paragraph (1), including the unauthorized acquisition, use, disclosure, or provision to another of the data assets, in a manner contrary to fair commercial practices or competitive order, or circumvention, removal, or alteration of the technical protection measures applied to the data assets without legitimate authority.
  (3) Matters regarding the unlawful use, etc. of data assets under paragraph (2) shall be governed by the Unfair Competition Prevention and Trade Secret Protection Act.

Article 13 (Support for information analysis utilizing data) (1) In order to promote data-driven information analysis, the Government may support programs necessary for the information analysis, such as data collection and processing.
  (2) Where data is used for information analysis, the protection and use of the works, etc. as defined in subparagraph 7 of Article 2 of the Copyright Act contained in the data shall be governed by that Act.

CHAPTER III PROMOTION OF DATA USE

Article 14 (Support for valuation) (1) The Minister of Science and ICT may establish and publish valuation methodologies and frameworks for assessing the value of data (excluding public data; hereafter in this Article the same shall apply) in order to facilitate the objective valuation of data.
  (2) The Minister of Science and ICT shall support the utilization of the valuation methodologies and frameworks under paragraph (1) in data-related transactions, finance, etc.
  (3) The Minister of Science and ICT may designate a data valuation institution to conduct the valuation of data in circulation in a professional and efficient manner (hereinafter referred to as "valuation institution").
  (4) A person who intends to have data valuated may file an application with a valuation institution designated under paragraph (3).
  (5) A valuation institution that receives an application for valuation under paragraph (4) shall conduct a valuation of the data and notify the applicant of the results without delay.
  (6) A valuation institution shall notify the Minister of Science and ICT of its data valuation information for the relevant year by the end of January of the following year, except where special circumstances prescribed by Presidential Decree exist, such as the maintenance of business or operational confidentiality.
  (7) The head of a valuation institution shall consult with the Minister of Science and ICT on the following matters:
  1. Subject of valuation;
  2. Scope of valuation;
  3. Fees of valuation.
  (8) Matters necessary for designation criteria and procedures for valuation institutions and application procedures for valuation shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 15 (Facilitation of data transfer) The Government shall endeavor to establish an institutional foundation that facilitates the smooth transfer of data by individuals to themselves or to third parties in a form that can be processed by information processing devices, such as computers, thereby facilitating the production, transaction, and utilization of data.

Article 16 (Reporting by data service providers) (1) The following service providers shall file a report with the Minister of Science and ICT. The same shall also apply to any modification of the reported matters:
  1. Data transaction service provider;
  2. Data analytics service provider.
  (2) The Minister of Science and ICT and the heads of relevant central administrative agencies may provide necessary financial and technical support, etc. to service providers that have reported under paragraph (1).
  (3) Matters necessary for standards, procedures, etc. for reporting under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Science and ICT.

Article 17 (Establishment of fair distribution environment) (1) The Minister of Science and ICT shall establish a fair competitive environment and promote mutual cooperation between large enterprises and small and medium enterprises in data transaction.
  (2) A data service provider prescribed by Presidential Decree shall not coerce an unfair contract or obtain unjust enrichment by exploiting its position, such as demanding the unilateral transfer of intellectual property rights related to data, without reasonable reasons.
  (3) The Minister of Science and ICT may request the head of a relevant agency to take necessary measures when the Minister deems that a data service provider is engaged in an act, in violation of paragraph (2).
  (4) The Minister of Science and ICT may perform the following projects to establish a fair competitive environment in the data transaction market:
  1. Analysis and evaluation of the current status of the data transaction market;
  2. Composition and operation of a consultative body involving data transaction-related service providers, etc.;
  3. Surveys on the actual use of standard contract forms;
  4. Other projects necessary for the establishment of a fair competitive environment.

CHAPTER IV PROMOTION OF DATA DISTRIBUTION AND TRANSACTIONS

Article 18 (Establishment of data distribution and transaction system) (1) The Minister of Science and ICT may establish a data distribution and transaction system to activate data distribution and transaction, and may provide support necessary for laying a foundation for data distribution and transaction.
  (2) The Minister of Science and ICT may establish and operate a data distribution system to facilitate data distribution and transactions.
  (3) Methods and standards necessary to support the establishment of a foundation for data distribution and transaction under paragraph (1), and matters necessary for the operation of data distribution system under paragraph (2) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 19 (Support for data platforms) (1) The Government may undertake projects to support platforms that collect, process, analyze, and distribute data, as well as provide data-driven services.
  (2) Matters necessary for the support projects under paragraph (1), including the methods, content, and scope thereof shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 20 (Data quality management) (1) The Minister of Science and ICT may, in consultation with the Minister of the Interior and Safety, undertake quality certification and other projects necessary for quality management in order to enhance the quality of data.
  (2) The Minister of Science and ICT may provide all or part of the funds incurred by persons in conducting projects necessary for quality management under paragraph (1).
  (3) The Minister of Science and ICT may designate a certification institution to conduct data quality certification under paragraph (1).
  (4) A certification institution designated under paragraph (3) shall conduct quality certification in accordance with the quality standards prescribed by Presidential Decree where it receives an application for data quality certification.
  (5) Except as provided in paragraphs (1) through (4), the scope of quality certification, requirements for designating certification institutions, quality standards and quality management, and other necessary matters shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 21 (Standard contract forms) (1) The Minister of Science and ICT may prepare standard contract forms in consultation with the Fair Trade Commission for the reasonable distribution and fair transaction of data and recommend their use to data service providers.
  (2) Where establishing or amending the standard contract forms under paragraph (1), the Minister of Science and ICT shall hear the opinions of relevant trade associations and other interested parties as well as experts.

Article 22 (Request for submission of materials) The Minister of Science and ICT and the heads of relevant central administrative agencies may request data transaction service providers and data analytics service providers to submit materials, such as technical personnel and business performance records, for the purpose of promoting the data industry.

Article 23 (Support for training of certified data transaction specialists) (1) An individual with expertise in data transactions may file for registration as a certified data transaction specialist with the Minister of Science and ICT.
  (2) An individual who intends to file for registration as a certified data transaction specialist under paragraph (1) shall meet the criteria for experience and qualifications in data transactions as prescribed by Presidential Decree and shall complete the education prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (3) An individual registered under paragraph (1) shall perform consultation, advisory, and guidance services specialized in data transactions; and supporting services, including intermediary or brokering services for data transactions.
  (4) The Minister of Science and ICT may revoke the registration of a certified data transaction specialist if any of the following applies to the specialist; provided, in the case of subparagraph 1, the designation shall be revoked:
  1. Where the specialist obtains the registration by fraud or other improper means;
  2. Where the specialist performs the services under paragraph (3) by false or other improper means;
  3. Where the specialist allows another to use his or her registered name.
  (5) The Minister of Science and ICT may provide certified data transaction specialists with necessary support, such as information provision and education required for the performance of data transaction services, in connection with policy measures to develop data professionals under Article 25.

CHAPTER V ESTABLISHMENT OF FOUNDATION FOR DATA INDUSTRY

Article 24 (Support for business start-up) (1) The Government may provide the following support to promote the data-driven industry and to strengthen enterprises' capabilities in data production, transaction, and utilization:
  1. Identification and implementation of initiatives for the development of data-driven products and services, and operation of testbeds;
  2. Implementation of education programs to strengthen the technical capabilities of data-driven enterprises;
  3. Support to promote the data industry investment ecosystem;
  4. Administrative support related to counseling for prospective entrepreneurs, entrepreneurs, or enterprises in data-related fields;
  5. Support for the identification and commercialization of excellent data-driven ideas;
  6. Other matters prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (2) The Government shall endeavor to foster data-specialized enterprises that possess technologies related to data production, transaction, and utilization.

Article 25 (Fostering of specialized personnel) (1) The Minister of Science and ICT and the Minister of the Interior and Safety shall establish policy measures for the following matters to develop data professionals:
  1. Basic direction for policies to develop data professionals and measures to utilize them;
  2. Measures relating to the development and utilization of education and training programs for data professionals;
  3. Measures for cooperation with academia, industry, and public institutions for the development of data professionals;
  4. Measures to support job creation and employment linkage for data professionals;
  5. Measures to support the establishment of data-related job standards and the stabilization of qualifications and new occupational categories.
  (2) The Minister of Science and ICT and the Minister of Interior and Safety shall endeavor to ensure that education and training conducted in accordance with the policy measures under paragraph (1) conform to the qualification system under Article 6 of the Framework Act on Qualifications.
  jq
  (4) Where education and training for the development of data professionals conducted by training institutions designated under paragraph (3) constitutes vocational skill development training under the National Lifelong Vocational Skills Development Act, the State shall subsidize training fees in accordance with the relevant statute.
  (5) Matters necessary for the designation, operation, and revocation of designation, of training institutions under paragraph (3) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 26 (Promotion of technological development and support for pilot projects) (1) The Minister of Science and ICT shall establish and implement support policy measures to promote private-sector research and development of data-related technologies and encourage increased investment in research and development, in connection with the advancement of technological development relating to the production, transaction, and utilization of data.
  (2) The policy measures prescribed in paragraph (1) shall include the following matters:
  1. Objectives for the development of technologies and plans for industrial application thereof;
  2. Securing of investment resources to promote technological development;
  3. Measures to implement research and development programs for technological development and to foster collaborative research and interdisciplinary research among industry, academia, and public institutions;
  4. Expansion of research infrastructure, including technical research personnel, facilities, and information;
  5. Promotion of international cooperation;
  6. Dissemination of research outcomes and technology transfer.

Article 27 (Fact-finding surveys) (1) The Minister of Science and ICT may conduct an annual survey on the status and actual conditions of the data industry infrastructure and data transactions and publish the results in order to promote industries based on data transaction and utilization and efficiently formulate and implement policy measures and plans under this Act.
  (2) When necessary for conducting a fact-finding survey under paragraph (1), the Minister of Science and ICT may request relevant materials (except for matters regarding public data) from the head of a relevant central administrative agency, the head of a local government, or the head of a public institution. In such cases, the head of the relevant central administrative agency, the local government, or the public institution in receipt of the request for materials shall comply with the request unless special circumstances exist not to do so.
  (3) The Minister of Science and ICT may request cooperation from data service providers or any other relevant institutions or organizations regarding matters necessary for conducting fact-finding surveys under paragraph (1).
  (4) The Minister of Science and ICT may request a specialized institution prescribed by Presidential Decree to conduct fact-finding surveys under paragraph (1).
  (5) The scope and methods of fact-finding surveys under paragraph (1) and other necessary matters shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 28 (Promotion of standardization) (1) The Minister of Science and ICT may, in consultation with the Minister of the Interior and Safety, establish and publicly notify standardization criteria for the following matters in order to facilitate the combination, transaction, and utilization of data in various products and services by ensuring the compatibility of data; provided, with regard to the matters for which the Korean Industrial Standards have been established under the Industrial Standardization Act, the Standards shall apply, and in cases of the enactment, amendment, etc. of the Korean Industrial Standards, the provisions of that Act shall apply accordingly:
  1. Data storage formats and transfer protocols;
  2. Data classification schemes;
  3. Other matters necessary for the combination, transaction, and utilization of data.
  (2) The Minister of Science and ICT may implement projects necessary for data standardization, including conducting studies, research and development for data standardization and establishing of cooperative systems with the international organizations for standardization.

Article 29 (Promotion of international cooperation) The Minister of Science and ICT shall identify global trends in the data industry and promote international cooperation with foreign governments, international organizations, or foreign companies and organizations.

Article 30 (Tax incentives) (1) For the promotion of the data industry, the State or a local government may reduce or exempt national taxes or local taxes related to the implementation of related projects, as prescribed by the Act on Restriction on Special Cases concerning Taxation, the Act on Restriction on Special Cases concerning Local Taxation, and other tax-related statutes and municipal ordinances.
  (2) The State or a local government may provide subsidies or make long-term loans to data service providers only in cases prescribed by Presidential Decree if necessary for achieving the purposes of this Act.
  (3) The Minister of Science and ICT may provide necessary administrative support in connection with the measures referred to in paragraphs (1) and (2).

Article 31 (Special support for small and medium entrepreneurs) (1) When implementing various support policy measures related to the data industry under this Act, priority consideration shall be given to small and medium entrepreneurs under Article 2 of the Framework Act on Small and Medium Enterprises (hereafter in this Article referred to as "small and medium entrepreneurs").
  (2) The Government shall endeavor to encourage the participation of small and medium enterprises in the data industry and shall reflect related matters in the implementation plans.
  (3) The Minister of Science and ICT may implement programs that provide partial financial assistance to small and medium entrepreneurs for expenses necessary for the transaction, processing, etc. of data in order to promote the data industry.
  (4) The Government may provide consulting support to data service providers that are small and medium entrepreneurs for the improvement of management, technology, finance, accounting, personnel system, etc.

Article 32 (Designation and operation of specialized institutions) (1) When necessary for efficiently supporting the establishment of a foundation for the data industry as a whole and the fostering of related industries, the Government may designate an institution to professionally perform the affairs (hereafter in this Article referred to as "specialized institution").
  (2) The specialized institutions may conduct projects designated as their duties, or entrusted to them, under this Act or any other statute or regulation as well as projects necessary for promoting data distribution and utilization and establishing an industrial foundation.
  (3) The Government may make contributions, loans, etc. to the specialized institutions to cover all or part of the funds required for performing the duties related to establishing the foundation for the industry as a whole and fostering related industries.
  (4) Matters necessary for the designation and operation of specialized institutions shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 33 (Establishment of association) (1) Data service providers may establish an association subject to the authorization of the Minister of Science and ICT, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, for purposes including improving operations related to the data industry, cooperating in the technological development, fostering a culture of data transactions and utilization.
  (2) The association shall be a legal entity, and except as otherwise provided in this Act, the provisions of the Civil Act governing incorporated associations shall apply mutatis mutandis with regard to the association.
  (3) Matters relating to the qualifications of members, the executive officers, the affairs, etc. of the association shall be provided in the articles of association; and other matters to be included in the articles of association shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (4) When the Minister of Science and ICT grants authorization under paragraph (1), the Minister shall publicly announce the fact and may partially entrust tasks prescribed by this Act to the association as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

CHAPTER VI DISPUTE MEDIATION

Article 34 (Establishment and composition of Data Dispute Resolution Committee) (1) A data dispute resolution committee (hereafter in this Chapter referred to as the "committee") shall be established to mediate disputes relating to the production, transaction, and utilization of data; provided, disputes arising in relation to the refusal or suspension of public data provision shall be governed by the Act on Promotion of the Provision and Use of Public Data and the Act on the Promotion of Data-Based Administration; disputes arising in relation to personal information shall be governed by the Personal Information Protection Act; and disputes arising in relation to copyright shall be governed by the Copyright Act.
  (2) The committee shall be composed of not less than 15 and not more than 50 members, including 1 chairperson.
  (3) Members shall be appointed or commissioned by the Minister of Science and ICT from among the following persons, and the chairperson of the committee shall be elected among and by the members:
  1. Individuals who currently hold or have held a position at or above the rank of associate professor at a university or accredited research institute, with a major in a field related to the production, transaction, and utilization of data;
  2. Current or former Grade IV public officials or higher (including members in general service of the Senior Executive Service), or individuals who hold or have held a position equivalent thereto in a public institution, with experience in duties related to the production, transaction, and utilization of data;
  3. Individuals qualified as a judge, prosecutor, or attorney-at-law;
  4. Individuals recommended by organizations related to the field of data among non-profit, non-governmental organizations defined in Article 2 of the Assistance for Non-Profit, Non-Governmental Organizations Act;
  5. Other individuals who have knowledge and experience in the production, transaction, and utilization of data, and dispute mediation.
  (4) Members shall serve on a non-standing basis, with a term of 3 years, and may be reappointed only once.
  (5) No member shall be removed or dismissed from office against the member's will, except in any of the following cases:
  1. Where the member is sentenced to the suspension of qualification or a heavier punishment;
  2. Where the member becomes unable to perform duties due to physical or mental incapacity;
  3. Where the member commits misconduct in connection with his or her duties;
  4. Where the member is deemed unsuitable to serve as a member due to neglect of duty or injury to dignity;
  5. Where the member fails to recuse himself or herself despite being subject to any of the subparagraphs of Article 36(1) or the former part of paragraph (2) of that Article.
  (6) A secretariat may be established if necessary for supporting the work of the committee.
  (7) Except as provided in paragraphs (1) through (6), matters necessary for the organization, operation, etc. of the committee shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 35 (Mediation of disputes) (1) A person seeking remedies for damages or mediation of disputes in relation to the production, transaction, and utilization of data may apply to the committee for mediation of the disputes; provided, this excludes cases where dispute the mediation has already been completed in accordance with other statutes.
  (2) Mediation shall be conducted by a mediation panel consisting of up to 3 members (hereinafter referred to as the "mediation panel"); provided, if the committee resolves that a case shall be mediated by the committee, the committee shall conduct the mediation.
  (3) The members of the mediation panel shall be designated for each case by the chairperson from among the members of the committee, but at least 1 person meeting the criteria under Article 34(3)3 shall be included.
  (4) The committee or the mediation panel shall prepare a settlement proposal within 45 days after receipt of an application for dispute mediation under paragraph (1), and recommend it to the parties to the dispute (hereinafter referred to as the "parties"); provided, where it intends to extend that period due to unavoidable circumstances, it shall notify the parties thereof, specifying the reasons therefor and the new deadline.
  (5) The settlement proposal under paragraph (4) may include restoration to the original state, compensation for damages, and any other measures necessary to remedy the harm, to the extent not inconsistent with the purport of the application.
  (6) Each of the parties that has received a recommendation under the main clause of paragraph (4) shall notify the committee or the mediation panel of whether it consents to the settlement proposal, within 15 days from the date of receipt of the recommendation. In this regard, if the party fails to express its intention within 15 days, it is deemed to have refused the settlement proposal.
  (7) Except as provided in paragraphs (1) through (6), matters necessary for the mediation procedures shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 36 (Exclusion, challenge, and recusal of committee members) (1) If any of the following subparagraphs applies to a member of the committee, the member shall be excluded from the mediation of the relevant case:
  1. Where a member or his or her current or former spouse becomes a party to the case or is in the relationship of a joint titleholder or co-obligor with a party to the case;
  2. Where a member is a current or former relative of a party to the case;
  3. Where a member has testified or provided appraisal regarding the case;
  4. Where a member is or has been involved in the case as an agent for a party to the case.
  (2) Where the circumstances indicate that it would be impractical to expect fair deliberations or determinations from a member, any party may file with the committee an application for a challenge to the member, and the committee shall decide on the challenge by resolution. In such cases, the member subject to the challenge shall not participate in the resolution.
  (3) Where a member falls under the circumstances described in paragraph (1) or (2), the member shall recuse himself or herself from the mediation of the relevant case.

Article 37 (Request for materials) (1) The committee may request the parties or persons for reference to provide materials necessary for dispute mediation. In such cases, the relevant party shall comply with such request unless good cause exists not to do so.
  (2) The committee may, if it deems necessary, require the parties or persons for reference to attend a meeting of the committee to hear their opinions.

Article 38 (Effect of mediation) (1) Mediation shall be concluded in any of the following cases:
  1. Where the parties have agreed to the settlement proposal under Article 35(4);
  2. Where the parties submit a mediation agreement to the committee.
  (2) Where mediation is concluded under paragraph (1), the committee shall send to the parties a written settlement agreement signed and sealed by the committee chairperson and each party.
  (3) The written settlement agreement under paragraph (2) shall have the same effect as a court settlement under the Civil Procedure Act.
  (4) The committee shall notify the parties that mediation has not been concluded in any of the following cases:
  1. Where an application for mediation is withdrawn, or either of the parties refuses to participate in the mediation of the dispute;
  2. Where a party rejects a settlement proposal of the committee.

Article 39 (Refusal and suspension of mediation) (1) The committee may refuse to conduct mediation in any of the following cases:
  1. Where dispute mediation has been completed in accordance with other statutes;
  2. Where it is deemed unsuitable for the committee to conduct mediation in light of the nature of the case;
  3. Where the application for dispute mediation is deemed to have been filed for an improper purpose.
  (2) The committee may suspend mediation if a party files a lawsuit before the mediation of the dispute is concluded.
  (3) Where the committee refuses mediation under paragraph (1) or suspends mediation under paragraph (2), it shall notify the parties of the fact and reasons therefor.

Article 40 (Mediation costs) (1) The committee may require persons who have filed an application for dispute mediation to bear the mediation costs, as prescribed by Presidential Decree; provided, if mediation is concluded, the committee may require the parties to the dispute to apportion the mediation costs based on the outcome of the mediation.
  (2) The Government may contribute expenses incurred for the operation of the committee within the budget.

Article 41 (Confidentiality) No person engaged or formerly engaged in the dispute mediation work of the committee shall disclose to any other person any secrets learned in the course of his or her duties nor shall use them for any purpose other than that of his or her duties; provided, this shall not apply where otherwise provided in other statutes.

CHAPTER VII SUPPLEMENTARY PROVISIONS

Article 42 (Claims for damages) (1) A person whose business interests are infringed upon and who suffers damages due to a violation of this Act may claim compensation for damages against a person who has committed the violation. In such cases, the violator shall not be exempted from liability unless he or she proves the absence of intent or negligence on his or her part.
  (2) Where the occurrence of damages is acknowledged but the amount of damages is difficult to calculate, the court may recognize a reasonable amount of damages, considering the purpose of the arguments and the results of the evidentiary investigation.

Article 43 (Guarantee of compensation for damages) A data service provider may take necessary measures, such as purchasing insurance, joining a mutual aid fund, or accumulating reserves, to fulfill its liability to compensate damages under Article 42.

Article 44 (Recommendation for correction) The Minister of Science and ICT may recommend necessary corrective measure to a data service provider that has violated this Act to cease or rectify the violation.

Article 45 (Legal fiction as public officials for purposes of applying penalty provisions) Any of the following persons shall be deemed a public official for purposes of applying the penalty provisions of Articles 129 through 132 of the Criminal Act:
  1. Executive officers and employees of specialized institutions defined in Article 32;
  2. Members of the data dispute resolution committee, or executive officers or employees of the secretariat under Article 34(6);
  3. Executive officers and employees of an institution or organization engaged in tasks entrusted under this Act.

Article 46 (Delegation or entrustment of authority) (1) The authority of the Minister of Science and ICT under this Act may be partially delegated to the heads of affiliated agencies, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (2) The authority of the Minister of Science and ICT under this Act may be partially entrusted to the institutions or organizations publicly notified by the Minister of Science and ICT as those having expertise in the production, transaction, and utilization of data, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

CHAPTER VIII PENALTY PROVISIONS

Article 47 (Penalty provisions) A person who divulges classified information that he or she has learned in the course of duties to other persons or uses it for a purpose other than official purpose shall be punished by imprisonment with labor for not more than one year or by a fine not exceeding 10 million won.

Article 48 (Administrative fines) (1) A person who uses the quality certification mark or any similar mark without obtaining quality certification under Article 20(4) shall be subject to an administrative fine not exceeding 30 million won.
  (2) Administrative fines under paragraph (1) shall be imposed and collected by the Minister of Science and ICT, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
